library-maps-tell-1: A map shows places with marks.
library-maps-tell-2: A key tells us what the marks mean.
library-maps-tell-3: A scale helps us compare distances.
library-maps-more-1: A map uses shapes, colors, and symbols to show places.
library-maps-more-2: A key explains what the symbols mean.
library-maps-more-3: A scale helps connect a distance on the map to a distance in the real world.
library-maps-more-4: A blue line might represent a river on one map.
library-maps-more-5: Check that map's key rather than assuming every color or symbol always has the same meaning.
library-maps-more-6: Our illustrated expedition map is a simplified learning map, not a navigation chart.
library-maps-deep-1: Maps are made for different jobs.
library-maps-deep-2: A walking map may show paths, while a weather map shows air conditions.
library-maps-deep-3: Our illustrated expedition map is a simplified learning map, not a navigation chart.
library-maps-deep-4: Mapmakers choose which details suit a purpose and scale.
library-maps-deep-5: A small-scale map covers a broad area with less local detail, while a larger-scale map can show smaller features.
library-maps-deep-6: Symbols let a point or line stand for something too small or complicated to draw at its real size.
library-maps-deep-7: A scale connects measured map distance with distance on the ground.
library-maps-deep-8: A key explains symbols, while orientation explains direction; these tools answer different questions.
library-maps-deep-9: The Library's illustrated map helps explore ideas and relationships, but it must not be used to navigate a real trip.

library-directions-tell-1: North, east, south, and west are directions.
library-directions-tell-2: A map can show them with arrows.
library-directions-tell-3: North is not always at the top.
library-directions-more-1: North, east, south, and west are directions.
library-directions-more-2: A compass rose on a map shows how the map is oriented.
library-directions-more-3: Many maps put north at the top, but not all do.
library-directions-more-4: A compass rose shows directions on a map.
library-directions-more-5: Turn the paper, and its printed arrows turn too, so check the arrows rather than guessing from the page edge.
library-directions-more-6: Use real navigation tools with a knowledgeable grown-up.
library-directions-deep-1: A magnetic compass points toward magnetic north, which is not exactly the same as the geographic North Pole.
library-directions-deep-2: A map may show different north arrows.
library-directions-deep-3: Use real navigation tools with a knowledgeable grown-up.
library-directions-deep-4: Geographic north points toward Earth's North Pole along a line of longitude.
library-directions-deep-5: Magnetic north is the direction a magnetic compass responds to, and it can differ from geographic north.
library-directions-deep-6: The difference is called magnetic declination and depends on place and time.
library-directions-deep-7: Some maps also show grid north, which follows their printed coordinate grid.
library-directions-deep-8: These arrows need not line up exactly.
library-directions-deep-9: An old map's magnetic information may therefore be out of date.
library-directions-deep-10: For a pretend map, choosing north-up is a useful convention; real navigation needs current information and a knowledgeable grown-up.

library-volcanoes-tell-1: Melted rock below ground is magma.
library-volcanoes-tell-2: At the surface it is called lava.
library-volcanoes-tell-3: A volcano lets material reach the surface.
library-volcanoes-more-1: Melted rock below the ground is called magma.
library-volcanoes-more-2: When it reaches the surface, it is called lava.
library-volcanoes-more-3: A volcano is an opening where material from inside Earth can reach the surface.
library-volcanoes-more-4: The same melted rock has a different name depending on where it is.
library-volcanoes-more-5: A cross-section drawing helps show the underground part that we cannot see from outside.
library-volcanoes-deep-1: Volcanoes do not all erupt in the same way.
library-volcanoes-deep-2: Some build islands and mountains over many eruptions.
library-volcanoes-deep-3: Many occur near plate boundaries, but some form over hot spots within a plate.
library-volcanoes-deep-4: A vent is an opening, and underground cracks can connect it to places where molten or partly molten rock is stored.
library-volcanoes-deep-5: Eruptions can release lava, broken rock, and gases, with very different patterns and durations.
library-volcanoes-deep-6: Repeated flows and deposits can build a mountain, but the visible cone is only part of a volcanic system.
library-volcanoes-deep-7: Plate boundaries explain many volcano locations, while hot spots help explain some others within plates.
library-volcanoes-deep-8: A simple cutaway shows one possible arrangement, not a diagram of every volcano.
library-volcanoes-deep-9: Learning about a volcano here does not supply current hazard or evacuation information.
